hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt with 44pc, three seats short of a majority
brief.h: The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of the Landtag's 83 seats on Sunday against the CDU's 17.2 per cent and 15 seats, on turnout that jumped from about 60 per cent to about 80 - leaving the four firewall parties holding exactly 39 seats between them and the five-seat BSW as the only bloc that can break the tie.
brief.t: Everyone will tell you today that the firewall held. Look at the ballot rule instead. A cordon sanitaire is a coalition instrument: it denies a party partners, and it does absolutely nothing about arithmetic. Saxony-Anhalt elects its Minister-President by secret ballot, absolute majority required in the first two rounds - which nobody has - and then a THIRD round decided by a simple majority of votes cast. In a chamber split 39 AfD, 39 firewall, 5 BSW, that third round can be won by a party that persuades nobody and simply waits for five people to abstain. The CDU has ruled out both the AfD and Die Linke, which means the 39 on the other side is not a bloc, it is four parties that have already excluded each other's arithmetic. This is why the ledger raised its AfD Minister-President question from 16 to 23 per cent today - the largest single move this book has made - and why it did not go higher: Ulrich Siegmund has said he will not stand without a stable majority, and seventy-seven years of German state politics contain zero AfD Minister-Presidents. The number that decides it is five.
brief.context: The rail here predates the headline by a long way: German Land constitutions were written after 1949 to make governments formable, which is why most of them contain a relative-majority fallback - a rule designed to prevent Weimar-style deadlock that now functions as the door the deadlock walks through. The desk that decides is not the federal CDU presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag's presiding officer running ballots, and the BSW's five-member group deciding whether to be in the room. Framework: Tsebelis on veto players - a norm binds only while the actors sustaining it have something to lose, and a Land party facing a repeat election it would likely lose again has less to lose each time. The base rate is the honest anchor and it is brutal: across 77 years and sixteen Laender, an AfD or predecessor far-right Minister-President has been sworn in zero times, and the closest analogue - Thuringia 2020, where an FDP candidate was briefly elected with AfD votes - collapsed within days under federal pressure, which is evidence that the informal enforcement is real and fast. Influence map: PRINCIPAL the Saxony-Anhalt electorate, AGENT the Landtag, NARRATOR the AfD leadership converting a plurality into a mandate claim, OPERATOR the BSW group whip, MARKET the German bund and the mid-cap industrial base, TARGET the CDU's federal coalition, which faces Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in thirteen days. Falsifier for the raise: a conventional coalition or a stable CDU-led minority government seated in Magdeburg within 90 days sends this question back to 16 and scores the move a miss.

consp.claim: That the count was rigged - claims of ballot-handling irregularities, miscounted postal votes and vote-rigging spread through German-language social media within hours of the polls closing, alongside a mirror-image claim from the other direction that the result itself was engineered by Moscow.
consp.spread: Loud on German-language X and Telegram overnight, amplified by AfD-aligned accounts; DW's fact-check desk traced a portion of it to Matryoshka, also called Operation Overload, the Russian-linked influence operation that has targeted previous German votes.
consp.read: This maps onto the stolen-election frame that has now been ported into four European electorates, and the interesting thing is that here it is being run by the WINNER, which is the tell that its purpose is mobilisation rather than reversal - a fraud narrative pre-loaded for the next vote, in thirteen days. The checkable kernel is small and specific: German Land elections are counted by volunteer local boards with party observers present and results are reconcilable at the precinct level, so a claim of systematic miscounting is unusually easy to test and unusually easy to make. What it is downstream of is the second claim being true in a limited way - Matryoshka is documented, which does not make the AfD's 43.9 per cent anything other than 43.9 per cent of real ballots.

angles.effect: GAINS by converting 43.9 per cent into the sentence 'the voters rejected the firewall' - a plurality restated as a mandate, thirteen days before two more elections
PAYS twice - it lost 25 seats and it is now the party that must either break its own taboo on Die Linke or explain why the state has no government
GAINS the highest-value five seats in Germany, because a third-ballot rule turns abstention into an appointment power
PAY if the arithmetic ends in repeat elections - the outcome in which the highest turnout in a generation produces no government at all

dec.kill: Whether the firewall parties lost seats on NET and whether any of them changes position in the formation talks. If a stable non-AfD government is seated, the mandate claim was rhetoric; if the CDU tolerates or the BSW abstains, it was a description.

brief.head: Brent nears $100 as Iran plans restricted zone beyond Hormuz
brief.h: Brent rose 1.2 per cent to $97.47 by midday London, after touching $97.93, its highest since 24 July, as Iran's Supreme National Security Council said it will declare a restricted maritime zone starting at the US Navy's blockade line and running through Gulf waters - with vessels that enter placed on a sanctions list - days after US Central Command struck three Iranian oil tankers including one near Kharg Island.
brief.t: Read the penalty, not the threat. Iran is not promising to sink the ships that enter its new zone; it is promising to LIST them. That is the whole story in one word. Guns are expensive, escalatory and reversible; a registry is cheap, deniable and permanent, and it works on the one actor that actually decides whether a hull sails - not a captain but an underwriter and a charterer, who will not touch a vessel that appears on anybody's list. Tehran is doing to the Gulf what it already did to the strait: converting a blockade it cannot break into a permit office it can administer, with Oman co-drawing the corridor maps so a neutral government's name is on the paperwork. The physical evidence says the coercion works even when the enforcement is thin - flows are running about 9 million barrels a day against 20 pre-conflict, and only 5 to 11 ships a day cross where more than 130 used to. The market is pricing the expansion: Brent is 2.5 per cent below the $100 line that resolves this board's Brent-band question on 24 September, and the ledger cut that question from 29 to 25 today on the geometry rather than on the mood.
brief.context: R0: this is a late chapter of the 1973-79 rail, but running through export CAPACITY rather than price - the lesson every producer learned in the embargo years was that the question is never the barrel in the ground, it is whether the cargo can be lifted, insured and invoiced. The historical mechanism has a name and it is older than oil: the Danish Sound Dues, three centuries of a state charging for passage through water it did not own, sustained not by superior navies but by the fact that paying was cheaper than fighting. The desk that decides here is not CENTCOM and not the SNSC - it is a war-risk syndicate at Lloyd's and a P and I club, and they move on incident frequency, not on declarations. Framework: Ostovar's thesis that the IRGC converts each crisis into a permanent institution, which is why this board's GEO-013 sits at 76 per cent on whether any eventual deal preserves Iranian transit administration. The base rate is unkind: after the Houthi campaign began in the Red Sea in late 2023, Bab al-Mandab transits more than halved and stayed depressed for well over a year, through announced reopenings - chokepoint traffic recovers on insurance repricing, which lags the politics by quarters. Stated falsifier, dated: if Iran has not published coordinates and Oman has not co-signed a corridor map by 22 September, the zone is a bargaining position rather than an administration and the escalation read is scored down, not deferred. Incompetence alternative, named as required: an SNSC that announces a zone it has no capability to police is performing for a domestic audience, and Stephen Zunes' point stands - Iranian assets attempting enforcement would be very vulnerable to US attack.

consp.claim: That specific strait incidents are staged or misattributed - that particular tanker casualties were arranged, or that mine and missile events were assigned to whichever side the reporting outlet disfavours.
consp.spread: Persistent rather than spiking, across X, Reddit and imageboards for months; the volume is high enough that Snopes maintains a standing collection of fourteen separately investigated Strait of Hormuz claims.
consp.read: This is the ordinary fog of a naval conflict where both belligerents are the only witnesses to their own incidents, and it maps onto the Gulf of Tonkin frame - which earns its place in the reference class rather than settling anything. The checkable kernel is real and cuts at both sides: in a shooting war on water, the party reporting an incident is usually the interested party, which is exactly why this board refused to count last week's Kharg report until the US military confirmed it. What it is downstream of is a genuine evidentiary vacuum - independent verification at sea requires imagery, salvage or an insurer entry, and all three arrive days late.

angles.effect: GAINS an instrument it can run without winning a naval battle - a list costs nothing to maintain and transfers the enforcement burden onto insurers and charterers
GAINS publishable results - three named hulls struck - and PAYS in a standing escort commitment, because a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
PAY the whole bill, in freight, insurance and a crude price 2.5 per cent under $100 that nobody in the Gulf is being asked to justify
GAINS the broker's rent it has earned in every Iran file since 2013, and PAYS by being the address blamed if the corridor fails

dec.kill: Published coordinates plus an Omani co-signature would make this an administration; two weeks of no map and no listed vessel would make it a bargaining position, and the board would score the escalation read down.

brief.head: Japan sold US Treasuries to fund a record yen defence
brief.h: The yen strengthened as much as 1.4 per cent to 154.06 per dollar on Monday, its firmest since late February and past the peak of July's joint US-Japan intervention, after reporting that Tokyo likely liquidated part of its foreign securities - including US Treasuries - to finance a record 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, of currency defence in the month to 26 August.
brief.t: The important thing here is not the exchange rate, it is who Washington was protecting when it did something almost unheard of. In July the US Treasury joined a foreign government's currency intervention - buying yen with American reserves - and Scott Bessent separately pushed the Federal Reserve to widen the FIMA repo facility, a plumbing line that lets a foreign central bank borrow dollars AGAINST its Treasury holdings instead of selling them. Follow that: Japan is one of the largest foreign holders of US government debt, the ten-year is already at 4.77 per cent and the thirty-year at 5.25, and a forced Japanese seller during a heavy issuance calendar raises the interest bill on the world's biggest borrower. So the valve exists to stop an ally becoming a seller. That is not a favour, and it is not a secret - it is published infrastructure that had to be widened, which tells you the dependency is being actively managed. The ledger raised its yen-carry stress question from 24 to 29 today: the yen has covered nearly half the distance to our 147.2 barrier in four sessions with the Bank of Japan meeting on 18 September, and the one thing holding it back is a Federal Reserve that markets think will hike two days earlier.
brief.context: R0: E7, the weaponized-settlement epoch, running backwards. The familiar direction is Washington using dollar clearing as a weapon; here it is Washington building a facility so an ally does not have to sell dollars, which is the balance-of-financial-terror in its original Summers formulation - foreigners hold the Treasuries, the US holds the switch, and both are hostages. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board and Japan's Ministry of Finance FX desk, not the cabinet, and on the American side the New York Fed's FIMA counterparty list rather than the podium. The mechanism to keep: the carry trade is thirty years of the world borrowing yen at nothing and buying everything else with it, and it unwinds when Japanese rates rise, because the cheap leg stops being cheap. Base rate first: episodes of 8 per cent or more yen appreciation inside thirty days are rare but recurrent - August 2024, when the Nikkei fell 12.4 per cent in a session; the October-December 2022 intervention run; 1998. The August 2024 template needed BOTH legs, a Tokyo surprise and a dovish repricing of the Fed, and today exactly one is live, which is why the raise was five points and not fifteen. Falsifier: a BoJ hold on 18 September that sends the yen back through 158 scores the raise a miss.

consp.claim: That the July operation was never about the yen at all - that Washington intervened to stop Tokyo dumping roughly $1.2tn of US Treasuries, and that FIMA is a secret bailout of the American bond market dressed as an ally's currency defence.
consp.spread: Circulating hard on financial X and in macro newsletters since early August, with at least one outlet running the claim as a straight headline; it has now been picked up in mainstream analysis as a serious motive question rather than a fringe one.
consp.read: This one is unusual because the kernel is largely correct and the framing is what is wrong. The motive claim is close to the published record - Bessent had flagged Japanese bond-market spillover into Treasuries in January, and FIMA's explicit design purpose is to prevent disorderly sales by large foreign holders. What does not survive is 'secret': the facility is public, the intervention was jointly announced, and the debate is being conducted in Goldman notes and PIIE blog posts. The useful correction is the one a Peterson Institute writer made - calling this a secret bailout overstates what is essentially financial-market plumbing - and the analytically interesting residue is that a genuine dependency is being managed in public while being described as an act of friendship.

angles.effect: GAINS a lid on its own long-end yields without buying a single bond itself, and PAYS in the precedent that it will backstop an ally's currency
GAINS dollars without selling collateral, and PAYS repeated repo rollover - a defence that must be refinanced is a deepening obligation, not a one-off

brief.head: Israeli strikes kill 18 in south Lebanon over two days
brief.h: Overnight strikes killed 11 people including two infants in a south Lebanon village a day after raids killed seven, the deadliest two-day stretch since the June truce, with Israel saying it acted after intercepting rockets that Hezbollah publicly denies firing and after clearing tunnels under the Ali al-Taher ridge on Friday.
brief.t: The thing to hold onto here is the difference between a raid and a ridge. Israeli air strikes on south Lebanon have run all summer without becoming a campaign, which is why this board has held its Israel-Hezbollah question at 30 per cent for weeks. What is different is that the June truce has no verifier - no agreed monitor, no jointly published line - so each side grades its own compliance, and the attribution of the rockets is now itself disputed: Israel says it intercepted them, Hezbollah says it did not fire them, and there is no third party empowered to say which is true. That is the structural defect, not a detail. President Joseph Aoun's response tells you where the real leverage sits: he asked Washington, not Beirut's own army, to stop it. The ledger raised the question three points to 33 today, and it is worth being precise about what bought those points - the casualty tempo, not the ridge. The ridge was taken on Friday and Israel's own June security-zone map already claimed it, so treating it as new evidence would be re-pricing something the board should have priced in June.
brief.context: The rail is the 1949 armistice architecture and its 2006 successor, UN Resolution 1701, which created a line that nobody was empowered to adjudicate - and the June 2026 truce repeated the omission. Fortna's finding, from the largest quantitative study of ceasefire durability, is that ceasefires survive on three things: a demarcation line, a monitoring mechanism and a guarantor with something at stake. This truce has none of them in operating form, which is why the base rate is grim - ceasefires without monitoring break at roughly twice the rate of those with it, and the modal failure is exactly this pattern of grinding attrition rather than a declared collapse. The desk that decides is Israel's Northern Command plus the political need of a prime minister facing an election, not the cabinet as a whole; on the other side it is Hezbollah's military council weighing whether responding costs it more than absorbing. Influence map: PRINCIPAL the Israeli electorate, AGENT Northern Command, NARRATOR the defence minister announcing cleared tunnels on social media, OPERATOR the air wing, MARKET nothing prices this directly, which is part of why it persists, TARGET the returned villagers of Nabatieh who came home after June. Falsifier for the raise: fourteen days without a comparable multi-death strike day sends this back to 30, scored as a miss.

consp.claim: That the intercepted rockets were a pretext - that the launch either did not happen or was not Hezbollah's, manufactured to license an operation already planned around the ridge.
consp.spread: Circulating across Arabic-language X and Lebanese Telegram channels and picked up in Western commentary, seeded by the unusual fact that the denial is on the record: Hezbollah publicly disputed firing the rockets Israel says it intercepted.
consp.read: This maps onto the standard casus-belli frame, and the reason it has traction is not the theory but the evidentiary structure: a truce with no monitor means the only account of a launch comes from the party that says it intercepted it, which is the same self-graded sourcing this board refuses when the claimant is Tehran. The checkable kernel is narrow and real - interception debris, radar tracks shared with a third party, or a UNIFIL observation would settle it, and none has been offered. What it is downstream of is the missing verifier, which also means the alternative explanation is fully available: rockets fired by a smaller faction Hezbollah does not control would produce exactly this pattern of true denial and true interception.

angles.effect: GAINS a demonstrated security zone and a hawk-satisfying result before an election, and PAYS in a Lebanese state it says it wants stronger being weakened every time it acts instead of it
GAINS the argument that disarmament is suicide, which is the single best recruiting line available to it, and PAYS in dead constituents and villages emptied twice in a year

angles.party: President Aoun and the Lebanese army
angles.effect: PAY the most - asked to disarm a militia while unable to stop the strikes that justify the militia, and forced to ask Washington to do it for them

dec.kill: Whether any third party - UNIFIL, the US-chaired mechanism, or a published radar track - is ever given the standing to adjudicate a launch. Without a verifier, both stories remain unfalsifiable and the attrition continues by design rather than by accident.

brief.head: Ship fuel runs short as refiners strip every barrel for diesel
brief.h: Very-low-sulphur bunker fuel at Singapore, the world's largest ship-fuelling port, has risen about 76 per cent since the war began to roughly $825 a tonne, with Middle East fuel oil exports down 45 per cent year on year to 447,000 barrels a day, Russian exports at a record low 591,000 b/d in August, and stocks at Rotterdam and Fujairah about 30 per cent below three-year seasonal norms.
brief.t: This is the most consequential story on the board that nobody will report as a crisis, because it has no explosion in it. A barrel of crude is a menu, not a product: run it through a refinery and you get diesel, gasoline, jet and - at the bottom - residual fuel oil, which is what ships burn. When the diesel crack spread, the gap between crude and diesel, hits records the way it has this year, the refiner reconfigures to squeeze every possible litre of diesel out of the barrel, and the cheapest product at the bottom simply stops being made. So the shortage is not caused by refineries failing; it is caused by refineries succeeding at the more profitable thing. Layer on the supply side - Hormuz disruption, Houthi strikes in the Red Sea, Ukrainian drones on Russian refineries - and analysts have a 218,000 b/d deficit for the third quarter. The consequence does not appear at a pump. It appears as freight cost, passed down every supply chain until, as one analyst put it, some trade simply stops making economic sense. That is a tax on world trade levied by a spread, and the board's diesel-crack question was held at 32 per cent today precisely because this evidence is about the same conversion constraint the ledger already priced on Friday.
brief.context: R0: this is the refining-configuration rail, the least glamorous and most load-bearing machine in the energy system, and it has been misread the same way since 1973 - policy argues about crude while the binding constraint is conversion. The desk that decides is not OPEC and not the Fed; it is a refinery scheduler choosing a crude slate and a turnaround calendar, and those decisions respond in years while crude valves respond in weeks. The mechanism to keep: crack spreads are the price signal that reconfigures the barrel, and a record diesel crack is an instruction to stop making bunker fuel. Framework: Hirschman on substitutability - the pain of a supply cut depends on how easily the buyer can switch, and a container ship cannot switch fuels between ports, which is what converts a spread into a route decision. Base rate: previous bunker squeezes - the 2020 IMO sulphur transition, the 2022 diesel spike - resolved within two to four quarters through demand rationing and cargo rerouting rather than through new capacity, because new conversion units take three to five years. Falsifier, dated: if a named carrier publishes a service suspension or a numerical bunker surcharge before 15 December, this has stopped being a price story and become a trade-volume one; if it has not, the squeeze is being absorbed and the board's 32 per cent on the crack question is scored as the correct restraint.

watch: Whether the Saxony-Anhalt Landtag goes to a THIRD ballot for Minister-President and what the BSW's five seats do when it does. The first two ballots need an absolute majority that nobody has; the third needs a simple majority of votes cast, which abstention alone can deliver. Watch for a published understanding rather than a speech - a written toleration agreement is the artefact, and the CDU's simultaneous exclusion of Die Linke is what makes the alternative arithmetic fail.

Whether Brent CLOSES above $100 before 24 September. It printed $97.93 intraday today and this board's question resolves on a daily settle, not a touch - which is the difference between our first Brier score and a non-score. The barrier is 2.5 per cent away with about twelve sessions left, and realised volatility has been running near 60 per cent annualised.

Whether Iran publishes actual coordinates for its restricted zone and whether Oman co-signs a corridor map. An announcement that ships entering will be sanctions-listed is a registry, not a navy - and a registry is the cheaper and more durable instrument, which is precisely why it is the one to watch. Absence of coordinates within two weeks would say the zone is a bargaining position rather than an administration.

Whether Japan's September reserve figure shows a second month of foreign-securities sales, and whether FIMA repo usage rises instead. Those two lines are alternatives: borrowing against Treasuries and selling them have opposite effects on the American long end, and which one Tokyo picks tells you how much room the ally actually has. Also watch whether the US Treasury describes the arrangement in writing.

Whether the bunker squeeze converts into a route decision. Ship fuel at Singapore is up 76 per cent and stocks at Rotterdam and Fujairah sit 30 per cent under seasonal norms; the tell that it has stopped being a price story is a named carrier publicly dropping a service or adding a fuel surcharge with a percentage attached, rather than analysts warning that some trade will stop making sense.
lesson: Today's lesson is a media-literacy one, because the German result is going to be described to you in two ways that are both technically about the same number. When the AfD co-leader said the firewall had been DEFINITIVELY REJECTED BY THE VOTERS, watch the move: a plurality is being converted into a mandate. The party won 43.9 per cent, which is a genuinely large and genuinely democratic result - do not let anyone talk you out of that - but 43.9 per cent is not a majority of voters rejecting anything, and turnout rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, meaning more people voted for EVERYONE. William Riker called this heresthetic: you win not by changing minds but by changing what the vote is understood to be ABOUT, and 'the voters rejected the firewall' redefines a seat count as a referendum on a norm. The counter-technique arrived the same night from the other direction - DW's fact-checkers documented fraud and vote-rigging claims spreading through the Matryoshka network, the Russian-linked operation that has targeted German elections before, which is Paul and Matthews' firehose of falsehood: not one persuasive lie but many cheap ones, fast, so that the cost of checking exceeds the cost of believing. What both techniques exploit is that you want a simple story about what a number MEANS. So here is the discipline, and it is boring on purpose: the honest test of 'the firewall was rejected' is not rhetoric, it is whether the firewall parties lost seats on net and whether any of them actually changes position in the coalition talks that start now. That is an observable with a date on it, and it is why this board raised its AfD Minister-President question to 23 per cent on the ballot ARITHMETIC rather than on the mood.

quiz.q: The AfD won 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt and every other party refuses to govern with it. Why does the brief still call an AfD Minister-President arithmetically possible?
options: Because the AfD can appoint a Minister-President directly once it wins the most votes
Because a third ballot is decided by a simple majority of votes cast, so abstentions can let 39 beat a divided 39
Because the federal chancellor can install a Land government when talks fail
Because the firewall is a law and laws can be repealed by a plurality
quiz.why: A cordon sanitaire is a coalition instrument. It denies a party partners; it does nothing about a ballot rule. Saxony-Anhalt requires an absolute majority in the first two ballots and a simple majority of votes cast in the third - which means the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by doing nothing at all.

quiz.q: Iran says its new restricted zone will begin at the US Navy blockade line, and that ships entering will be put on a sanctions list. What does the brief say that choice of penalty reveals?
options: That Iran has run out of missiles and can only threaten paperwork
That Iran is building a legal and administrative instrument it can keep running after the shooting stops, not just a naval one
That the zone is a bluff with no enforcement behind it
That Iran intends to seize every vessel that enters
quiz.why: Guns are expensive and reversible; a registry is cheap and permanent. Afshon Ostovar's thesis about the IRGC is that it converts each crisis into an institution that outlives it - which is why the ledger carries a separate question, at 76 per cent, on whether any eventual Hormuz deal leaves Iranian transit administration standing.

quiz.q: Ship fuel is short while refineries are running hard. What is the mechanism the brief names?
options: Refineries are being sabotaged, so total output has collapsed
A record diesel crack makes it more profitable to squeeze every barrel into diesel, so the cheapest product in the barrel stops being made
Shipping demand has surged beyond any possible supply
Sanctions forbid the sale of marine fuel to commercial vessels
quiz.why: A barrel is a menu, not a single product. When the spread between crude and diesel hits records, the refiner reconfigures toward diesel and residual fuel oil - what ships burn - becomes the casualty. That is why the shortage shows up as a freight cost rather than as an empty pump.

quiz.q: The US Treasury joined a foreign currency intervention and pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility. What does FIMA actually let Japan do?
options: Print dollars directly through the Federal Reserve
Borrow dollars against its Treasury holdings instead of selling them
Buy US Treasuries at a discount to the market
Convert its reserves into gold held at the New York Fed
quiz.why: The whole point is to prevent a forced seller. If Tokyo liquidates Treasuries to buy yen, it pushes up the yield on the debt Washington has to roll - so the US built a valve that lets an ally raise dollars without dumping the collateral. Published plumbing, not a secret favour, but it exists because the dependency runs both ways.

quiz.q: CRITICAL THINKING. After the Saxony-Anhalt result, an AfD co-leader said the firewall had been definitively rejected by the voters. Which observable best tests that CLAIM?
options: Whether the AfD is the largest party in the chamber
Whether commentators say the firewall is finished
Whether turnout rose compared with the previous election
Whether the parties maintaining the firewall lost seats on net, and whether any of them actually changes its position in the government-formation talks that follow
quiz.why: The claim is about voters rejecting a policy, but the evidence offered is one party winning a plurality. Turnout rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, which means more people voted for everyone. The honest test is behavioural on both sides: did the firewall bloc shrink in net seats, and does any of its members break? A plurality of 44 per cent is a genuinely large mandate and should not be dismissed - it is simply not the same proposition as a rejected firewall.

plumbing.read: The plumbing story today is not the oil price, it is who paid for Japan's currency defence. Tokyo spent a record 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, in the month to 26 August, and Bloomberg now reports it likely funded part of that by selling US Treasuries. That is the mechanism this board has been describing in the abstract, arriving as a print: a foreign official holder liquidating reserve assets pushes up the yield on the very instrument the US must roll, at the exact moment the ten-year sits at 4.77 per cent and the thirty-year at 5.25. Washington saw it coming. The reason the US Treasury joined a currency intervention at all - an almost unheard-of act - and the reason Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, is that FIMA lets a foreign central bank borrow dollars AGAINST its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as what it is: a plumbing valve built to stop an ally from becoming a forced seller of American debt. It is not a secret bailout, it is published infrastructure - but the fact that it had to be widened tells you the balance-of-financial-terror is being actively managed rather than merely observed. The second-order effect lands on GEO-025, raised to 29 today: the yen has done half the distance to our carry-stress barrier in four sessions, and the BoJ meets on 18 September.
plumbing.epoch: E7, the weaponized-settlement rail, running in reverse for once. The usual direction is Washington using access to dollar clearing as coercion; today it is Washington building a facility so that an ally does not have to sell dollars, because the coercer needs the buyer. Alongside E1, the 1973-79 oil-and-dollar rail now expressed as export CAPACITY rather than price - a permit office at a strait, and a bunker market where refiners have stopped making the cheapest product in the barrel - and E6, whose September-2019 repo confession never closed: the Fed still buying bills, ON RRP at $0.68bn.

sections.t: US diesel set an all-time record this week at $5.820 a gallon, and the crack spread — the refiner's fee for turning crude into something an engine can burn — printed an all-time $108 a barrel while Brent sat at an unremarkable $96. In the same week US missiles reportedly struck a tanker at Iran's Kharg Island anchorage, and Ukrainian drones held Russian refinery runs at 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since May 2002.

Crude — the thing everyone photographs and embargoes — is behaving; refined product is not. A $108 crack means the market will pay more to convert a barrel than the barrel is worth: a fact about cokers and hydrotreaters, not about oil. Name the mechanism — the conversion bottleneck. The binding constraint is never the abundant input but the narrow step in the middle, which cannot be built on the timescale of a war or an election.

sections.h: Deep history I — Rockefeller never wanted the oil
sections.t: John D. Rockefeller owned almost no wells. He owned the refineries of Cleveland, and what he did with them in 1871 is the founding text of chokepoint economics. Tom Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad chartered the South Improvement Company, and Rockefeller's terms inside it were breathtaking: the Erie, New York Central and Pennsylvania would pay the SIC a rebate of $1.06 on every barrel it shipped — and a drawback of $1.06 on every barrel shipped by refiners outside the club. He was paid when his rivals did business. The charter was repealed that April before a single transaction cleared, and Ida Tarbell's exposé later finished the job — but the insight outlived the scandal: crude is worthless until someone converts and moves it, and whoever owns the narrow step prices the wide one.

sections.h: Deep history II — the war decided at the still
sections.t: The largest test of this proposition was the Allied air war, fought inside the alliance before it was fought over Germany. Arthur Harris of RAF Bomber Command believed in punishment: burn the cities, break the will. Carl Spaatz and Arthur Tedder pushed what Harris dismissed as panacea targets — oil. Germany had almost no crude. It had Bergius hydrogenation, synthetic fuel pressed from coal at Leuna, Pölitz and Brüx, plants too enormous to hide. The oil plan began in May 1944. Leuna alone absorbed 22 raids, 6,552 bomber sorties and 18,328 tons of bombs across a year, behind Europe's heaviest flak concentration. It worked anyway. German synthetic output fell from a peak of 316,000 tons a month to 107,000 in June 1944 and 17,000 by September. Aviation gasoline — the specific fraction, not oil in general — went from 175,000 tons in April to 5,000 in September: 97% gone in five months. From May 1944 Germany consumed more than it produced every month, and the stockpile was gone in six.

sections.h: Deep history II — the fuel, not the factories
sections.t: The detail that makes it unforgettable: over the same period Albert Speer drove German tank and aircraft PRODUCTION to its wartime peak. The Reich ended 1944 with more airframes than it could fly and more panzers than it could move — the factories were fine and the fuel was not. The US Strategic Bombing Survey — written by people with every reason to praise bombing in general — judged the oil and transport campaigns decisive and the city campaign not. Japan lost the same way: the July 1941 freeze is remembered as an oil embargo, but the fatal shortage was 100-octane aviation gasoline, a conversion capability Japan could not build.

sections.h: Deep history III — how the West stopped building stills
sections.t: Now the slow part. The last greenfield major refinery built in the United States was Marathon's Garyville, Louisiana: built 1973-76, online 1977, still running at 596,000 barrels a day. Fifty years, no new plants — and the base is now shrinking: about 132 operable refineries in January 2025 against more than 300 in 1981, with roughly 1.235m b/d of distillation capacity removed in seven recent closures and conversions, over 6.5% of the total. All of it while shale made America the largest crude producer in history at 13.86m b/d. The country built the well and stopped building the still. The capacity emigrated rather than vanished — Jamnagar runs 1.24m b/d, Dangote opened at 650,000 and plans 1.4m, China kept building — so the toll moved east and south, to jurisdictions happy to buy discounted sanctioned crude and sell the product back to the people imposing the sanctions.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: In all three cases the scarce thing is the transformation, and transformation capacity is inelastic over any politically relevant horizon: a new crude supplier takes a fortnight, a new hydrocracker takes five years and a billion dollars. Ukraine is now running the 1944 oil plan at a ten-thousandth of the cost, a drone flying 1,550km to Omsk doing what 6,552 B-17 sorties did to Leuna — Pape's denial thesis tested live. It breaks against me here: Germany had no crude and no neutral supplier, Russia has both, and a 24-year low in refining has not stopped Pokrovsk.

sections.h: The adjudication — Yergin and Blas vs Chris Miller
sections.t: THE ADJUDICATION — YERGIN AND BLAS versus CHRIS MILLER Yergin and Blas hold that energy chokepoints self-heal — inventories, bypass and rerouting absorb shocks forecast to be fatal — and they have been right about the barrel, Brent at $96 in a war that curtailed over 11m b/d. Chris Miller's Chip War argues the opposite for inputs that are not fungible: no reserve of fabs, no bypass for EUV, a decade to rebuild. The evidence splits them by step. Yergin and Blas won the crude argument; the crack is the market announcing the win does not survive one step downstream, because there is no strategic reserve of cokers — the US holds hundreds of millions of barrels of crude in the SPR and about a million barrels of distillate in the Northeast reserve, having stockpiled the input it cannot burn. Miller's case is still weaker in oil than in silicon: diesel is shippable in a way a fab's output is not, so refining heals in 12-24 months rather than 12-24 days.

OECD gasoline demand is in structural decline as EVs scale; diesel and jet demand are not, because trucks, ships, aircraft, mining and data-centre backup have no substitute. But a refinery makes every cut at once, so the economics that close Western refineries — falling gasoline — destroy the distillate capacity nobody meant to lose. A trap, not a cycle; confidence high. The bolder call, near 60%: by the mid-2030s the US is at once the world's largest crude exporter and a chronic net importer of middle distillates, and that buys a strategic PRODUCT reserve — legislated storage of diesel and jet, enacted after a winter shortage rather than before one. What keeps this honest is GEO-026: does the US diesel crack settle below $45 before 15 December 2026? It sits at 35%, so the house is 65% on regime rather than outage — and if the crack mean-reverts on the 2022 schedule, this is an elegant story about a spike, published as a miss.
